ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: At the bottom of the figure is a common wire; the upper-left node is labeled U1, and the upper-right node is labeled U2. An 8Ω resistor is connected between U1 and the bottom common line. The top branch between U1 and U2, from left to right, is successively a 2Ω resistor and a voltage source labeled +2V−, indicating that the voltage source drops 2V from left to right. A 4Ω resistor is connected between U2 and the bottom common line; on the right side there is also a 3A current source in parallel with the 4Ω resistor, with the arrow upward, indicating that 3A is injected into the U2 node. Reasoning: According to the specified method, take the bottom wire as 0V. Define the current in the top series branch flowing from U1 to U2 as I=(U1-U2-2)/2. Write KCL for the U1 node: U1/8 + (U1-U2-2)/2 = 0, which simplifies to 5U1 - 4U2 = 8. Write KCL for the U2 node: U2/4 + (U2+2-U1)/2 - 3 = 0, which simplifies to 2U1 - 3U2 = -8. Solve the two equations simultaneously: from 2U1 - 3U2 = -8, obtain U1=(3U2-8)/2; substituting into 5U1 - 4U2 = 8 gives 5(3U2-8)/2 - 4U2 = 8, that is, 3.5U2 = 28, so U2 = 8V.

method.method_draft: Take the bottom wire as 0 V. Define the current through the top series branch from U1 to U2 as I=(U1-U2-2)/2 because the 2 V source drops 2 V from left to right. Apply KCL at U1: U1/8 + (U1-U2-2)/2 = 0. Apply KCL at U2: U2/4 + (U2+2-U1)/2 - 3 = 0. Solve these simultaneous equations to obtain U2 = 8 V, so report 8.0.
